R0259.title: C2C Blind-Shipping Fraud
R0259.definition: In C2C scenarios, groups blind-ship parcels with cash-on-delivery to recipients who never placed orders, defrauding them of payment.
R0259.description:
C2C blind-shipping fraud sends parcels with cash-on-delivery to recipients who never placed orders, exploiting the pay-on-receipt mechanism to defraud them, often shipping low-value goods as high-value items.

The risk directly harms consumers, damages platform and logistics brand trust, and triggers complaints and regulatory pressure. Detection must combine shipper qualification, COD order behavior models, and recipient complaint clustering to intercept and trace blind shipments.
R0259.influence: C2C blind-shipping fraud directly causes consumer financial loss, damages platform and logistics brand trust, and triggers complaints, regulatory, and legal risks.

R0259-001.title: Blind-Sale Fraud
R0259-001.definition: The black-market term "blind-sale" refers to blind-shipping parcels with cash-on-delivery to recipients who never placed orders.
R0259-001.description:
Blind-sale fraud is the black-market variant of C2C blind-shipping fraud, where groups blind-ship parcels with cash-on-delivery without a real transaction, exploiting the pay-on-receipt mechanism.

The method is essentially identical to C2C blind-shipping fraud; the slang "blind-sale" emphasizes the "blind shipping/selling" pattern common in black-market discussion. Detection aligns with the parent risk: shipper qualification, COD order behavior, and recipient complaint clustering.
R0259-001.influence: Blind-sale fraud directly causes consumer financial loss, damages logistics and platform brand trust, and triggers complaints and regulatory risks.
